observations:
Torah #11 yields 7 packages from its 36 bechina edges and 50 nodes. All concepts in the bechina dataset are accounted for within the existing 7 packages. No isolated cluster emerged that could not be assigned to one of those 7 packages or merged into a neighboring one. The teaching's conceptual topology is fully mapped by the current packages.

The 7 packages map precisely onto Torah #11's own argumentative structure:
- Packages 1 and 2 (upper and lower unification) mirror the Shema/Baruch-Shem dyad and the Shabbat/weekday brit observance.
- Packages 1 and 2 are themselves the GOOD mirror of the eitza-chain: brit shmirah produces kavod produces speech produces teshuva produces Torah depth.
- Package 3 (speech/bird/Torah depth) is the central mechanism — the mediating bridge concept of the entire Torah.
- Package 4 (39/Mishkan) captures the dual-polarity structural metaphor at the heart of section Dalet.
- Package 5 (gaavah/avodah zarah) is the evil counterpart of the kavod-humility teaching.
- Package 6 (shmirat habrit beshte bechinos) synthesizes the two levels and adds the kedushat hazivug dimension.
- Package 7 (teshuva/yarka) is the practical output of illuminating speech.

The missing bechina edges identified in torah_11_additions.json (especially lines 50-53, the opening verse analysis) would strengthen the existing packages but do not create new ones. If those edges were added: 'Ani H' = yichuda ila'ah' would add to Package 1; 'Hu Shmi = yichuda tata'ah' to Package 2; 'utehilati lapesilim = dibur' to Package 3. All additions fit within existing package boundaries.

The only candidate for a potential independent package — not pursued — was the 'kavod bishleimut / anavah / katnut' cluster (humility, self-nullification, 'leit maya'), which appears extensively in eitza edges but has virtually no bechina edges of its own in Torah #11's dataset. This is a conceptual domain (humility/honor of Heaven) that functions primarily as a causal bridge (eitza: humility enables speech) rather than a thematic equivalence cluster (bechina). It therefore correctly appears in eitza edges and should not be forced into a bechina package.
